questions.q: What do we call two lines that cross each other at a single point?
questions.a: These are called intersecting lines. A student who says "parallel" reveals a fundamental confusion between lines that never meet and lines that cross.

questions.q: If two lines are perpendicular, what must be true about the angle they make?
questions.a: They must meet at a right angle (90 degrees). Answering "they just touch" ignores the specific requirement of the 90-degree turn, showing the student hasn't distinguished perpendicular lines from general intersecting ones.

questions.q: Two lines are drawn on a paper. One is horizontal and one is vertical. They meet at a corner. Are they parallel, intersecting, or perpendicular?
questions.a: They are perpendicular. A student who says "intersecting" is technically correct but incomplete; missing the "perpendicular" classification shows they aren't identifying the 90-degree property.

questions.q: If I extend two parallel lines for 1 kilometre, will they eventually meet? Why?
questions.a: No, they will never meet because they maintain a constant distance from each other. Answering "yes" suggests the student thinks parallel lines are just "lines that haven't met yet" rather than lines that are physically incapable of meeting.

questions.q: Look at the letter 'H'. Identify the relationship between the two vertical bars and the horizontal bar.
questions.a: The two vertical bars are parallel to each other, and the horizontal bar is perpendicular to both vertical bars. A student who misses the parallel relationship is not observing the relative positions of all parts of the shape.

questions.q: Draw a shape using only parallel and perpendicular lines. Explain your choice.
questions.a: A rectangle or a square is the best example. A poor answer (like a triangle) reveals the student doesn't understand that parallel/perpendicular lines require specific orientations that triangles don't consistently provide.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Lines are classified by their mutual position: parallel lines never intersect despite infinite extension, intersecting lines share exactly one common point, and ______ lines are a special case of intersecting lines that meet at a 90-degree angle.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a railway track and wondered why the two iron rails never ______ each other?
What is Lines? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Lines are classified by their mutual position: parallel lines never intersect despite infinite extension, intersecting lines share exactly one common point, and perpendicular lines are a special case of intersecting lines that meet at a 90-degree angle.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Lines are classified by their mutual position: parallel lines never intersect despite infinite extension, intersecting lines share exactly one common point, and perpendicular lines are a special case of intersecting lines that meet at a ______-degree angle.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Lines?
questions.a: Students often believe that if two lines are "close" to each other but don't touch on the paper, they are parallel.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to visually identify parallel, intersecting, and perpendicular lines in real-world objects and accurately draw them using a ruler and set-square.
